title: Add a new red (destructive-style) button
description: Ship a visible red action control in the Planstack sidebar (and optional Chat footer) with theme-aware colors, a single clear behavior, and the same postMessage pattern as existing toolbar buttons. Align with VS Code's danger/destructive affordances so it works in light and dark themes.

phases.title: Define placement and behavior
phases.description: Lock the UX: which surface (Overview toolbar in planstackSidebar.js, graph controls, and/or Chat webview), exact label, tooltip, and the user-visible outcome (e.g. opens an existing command, shows a confirmation, or no-ops for a placeholder).

tasks.desc: Write a one-paragraph spec: button label, target command or handler name, and whether a confirmation dialog is required
If the action is new, pick command id under hackupc.planstack.* and register it in package.json with activation; otherwise map to an existing command

phases.title: Sidebar markup and styling
phases.description: Add the button next to the existing top-toolbar / create buttons pattern in planstackSidebar.js, with a dedicated CSS class in planstackSidebarWebview.ts. Use var(--vscode-errorForeground) / related theme tokens (or a documented red) so the control reads as “dangerous” without hardcoding a single theme.

tasks.desc: Insert the button HTML in planstackSidebar.js (same toolbar region as + Plan / view switchers) and add .btn-danger (or similar) rules with hover/focus for accessibility
tasks.prompt:
Scope: markup and CSS only for this task. Do not wire postMessage or extension handlers (that is a later phase).

In extension/media/planstackSidebar.js, find the top toolbar where “+ Plan” and the list/graph view switchers are rendered. Add a <button type="button"> in that same toolbar row with a clear label (e.g. short destructive label or icon+tooltip via title=), a dedicated class such as btn-danger, and a placeholder data-action value reserved for later wiring (e.g. noop or a stub name documented in a short HTML comment).

In extension/src/ui/planstackSidebarWebview.ts, add styles for .btn-danger (or the class you chose) alongside existing sidebar toolbar button styles: foreground using theme tokens such as var(--vscode-errorForeground) and/or var(--vscode-inputValidation-errorForeground), border/background subtle enough for light and dark themes. Include :hover and :focus-visible states with a visible focus outline (e.g. outline or box-shadow using var(--vscode-focusBorder)) so keyboard users get a clear ring.

Keep narrow sidebar widths in mind: the new control must not overflow the toolbar; follow spacing/patterns of neighboring buttons.

tasks.desc: Verify layout in list and node views, and that the new control does not break narrow sidebar widths or graph toolbar overflow

phases.title: Wire click → extension action
phases.description: Route data-action in the webview’s click handler, postMessage to the extension host, and invoke vscode.commands or a small helper. Reuse the patterns used for runPhase, quickCreatePlan, and sync actions.

tasks.desc: Add the data-action branch in planstackSidebar.js and the corresponding message type handler in planstackSidebarWebview.ts (or the shared bridge module if applicable)
Log via getOutput from log.ts on invoke and handle failure (unknown workspace, command not found) with a user-visible error message

phases.title: Optional Chat parity and handoff
phases.description: If the product decision includes Planstack Chat, add a matching red control in planstackChatWebview.ts / planstackChat.js with the same command; if out of scope, document skip in the plan description and mark tasks cancelled.

tasks.desc: Either mirror the button in the Chat input footer (styled consistently) or set phase/task state to cancelled with a short note in task prompt why
